title: Minor: 'unique topological order' of condensation stated imprecisely

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Severity: minor (wording).**

In Section 3.1, after Lemma 2: "Because $\widehat D$ is acyclic, it has at most one Hamiltonian path, and it has one iff its unique topological order ... satisfies $C_{\sigma(j)}\to C_{\sigma(j+1)}$." An acyclic digraph need not have a *unique* topological order; uniqueness holds only *after* one knows a Hamiltonian path exists. Correct statement: an acyclic digraph has a Hamiltonian path iff *some* topological order has all consecutive arcs present, and in that case both the Hamiltonian path and the realising order are unique. The algorithmic check is correct; only the wording asserting a pre-existing "unique topological order" should be tightened. Not a substantive gap.
